strings.name: Morris Chang
strings.summary: After a technical and management career in the United States, Morris Chang moved to Taiwan and founded TSMC. He promoted manufacturing for external chip designers, separating design from fabrication. His career connects industrial research, high-volume production and global supply chains; he retired from TSMC in 2018.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2024, not an exhaustive news record. Institutional achievements are team efforts; announced plans are not completed results.
strings.influence.rationale: Founded TSMC and advanced the dedicated-foundry model, reshaping the division between chip design and manufacturing.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: MIT mechanical engineering BS, 1952, MS, 1953; Stanford electrical engineering PhD, 1964
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Dedicated chip foundry
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Built TSMC to manufacture chips for customers without their own fabrication plants.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Industrial specialization
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Advanced the separation of design and manufacturing, strengthening Taiwan’s semiconductor production role.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Autobiography sequel
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Published a second volume covering Texas Instruments and TSMC’s founding.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Retired from TSMC
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Ended his chairmanship and handed leadership to a new generation.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Returned as CEO
strings.timeline.event-3.text: TSMC’s board again appointed him CEO alongside his chairmanship.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Founded TSMC
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Established a Taiwan-based company dedicated to manufacturing customers’ chips.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Led ITRI
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Moved to Taiwan to lead its Industrial Technology Research Institute.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Stanford doctorate
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Completed a PhD in electrical engineering.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Joined Texas Instruments
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Advanced through technical and management roles, eventually leading global semiconductor operations.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Joined Sylvania
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Began semiconductor work at the U.S. electronics company.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: MIT master’s degree
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Earned a mechanical engineering master’s after his 1952 bachelor’s degree.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Ningbo
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Zhejiang; his early life included moves through Hong Kong and Shanghai.
